root.name: Ponziani Opening: Neumann Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. c3 Nf6 4. Bc4

overview: The position is the Italian Two Knights Defense with c3 played, reached by a Ponziani move order. Black takes the e4 pawn with 4...Nxe4 and White answers 5.d4, or Bxf7+ ideas, for development in an open centre. Because it so often transposes, this root is unsure; the play is open with White trying to regain the pawn with tempo.

white_ideas.idea: 5.d4 d5 and open the centre, regaining e4 with tempo
Pressure on f7 with Bc4 and Qb3 or Bxf7+

black_ideas.idea: Take the e4 pawn and keep it with ...d5 and ...Bd6
Return the pawn for a solid game with ...Be7 and ...O-O

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4, with pawns traded on e4 and d5

character.notes: Open, tactical play with White chasing quick development; unsure about exact branching.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the e4 pawn, but unsure; many lines return it or transpose.

soundness.notes: Considered sound but not better than equal.

structure.notes: Central pawns exchange quickly; open lines for pieces.

approach.notes: Seldom chosen by strong players; the Ponziani is occasional and this gambit more so.

sublines_that_differ.name: Italian Two Knights with c3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. c3
sublines_that_differ.how: Transposition seen in most games; same position after one more move order.

character.reason: Open centre and a pawn offer give forcing play.

gambit.reason: White offers the e4 pawn for development; unsure it is kept.

level.reason: Some tactics to know; no deep theory.

plans.reason: Bc4 aims at f7 and White develops fast.
